payload.headline: NVIDIA breaks support at 145.98 amid reported CEO exit; wait, no swing trade

summary.thesis: The business numbers are still very strong and the price is low against them, but the price only holds up if today's 65.21% operating margin lasts, and the reported leadership turmoil has pushed the stock below yesterday's support.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, because yesterday's failure trigger (a close below the support zone) has fired. Swing: no trade in a downtrend that has no support level below the price.
summary.act_at: Hold again on a close above 150.03; buy at 113.77

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 145.98, down 3.3% on the day. That is below the 147.57–150.03 zone, which was support yesterday and is now the nearest resistance (a ceiling where selling tends to appear). News reports say Jensen Huang has left as chief executive and that his and the company's legal exposure has grown. They also report that Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies and that NVIDIA expanded its work with Microsoft. No next earnings date is in our data, and the latest quarterly filing is dated 2026-08-26.
payload.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business itself. Latest-quarter sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. Net cash is 23.2B, so the balance sheet is not a risk. What is at risk is how long this lasts. The filings flag that the margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. They also show unpaid customer bills up 127% against sales up 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. The reported CEO exit, the legal exposure and the insider sales of $946.6M outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues for now. They do not change demand, margins or cash today. A leadership change can affect strategy and customer relationships over time (general knowledge). The reported China chip approvals could support demand, but they are not confirmed by a filing.

worth.text: At 145.98, the price assumes free cash flow starts growing about 19.1% a year and slows to 3% over ten years. The model values the company at 151.37 if growth starts at 20% and 220.46 if it starts at 30%, so the price is fair to cheap only if growth holds near those rates. The DCF (a model that values the company's future cash flows in today's money) gives 189.34 / 219.77 / 260.38 (bear / base / bull). These figures are held back because the model caps starting growth at 30%, while the company's actual growth figures are 83%, 110% and 70%. The method based on the company's own past price-to-sales ratios gives a higher 217.35–411.04, because NVIDIA traded at higher sales multiples in the past. Today's price-to-sales of 11.6 sits at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year history and below the peer median of 16.2. The 9.6x... figure aside, the forward price/earnings ratio is 8.8 times next year's estimated earnings. The biggest swing factor is margin, not growth. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 113.77, and at 32% it drops to 76.17. Note that the DATA valuation summary still quotes yesterday's 150.96 price.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, while free cash flow growth starts at 20% or more.

bull: Profits are expected to keep rising: next year's earnings estimate is 16.61 a share, up 27.7% in 90 days, which puts the stock at only 8.8 times next year's earnings.
Cash generation nearly doubled: trailing free cash flow is 127.0B against 72.0B a year earlier, with 23.2B of net cash.
The stock is cheap against its own past and its peers: price-to-sales of 11.6 is at the 4.0th percentile of its 5-year history and below the peer median of 16.2.
bear: The 65.21% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. If it fades to 48%, the model value is 113.77, well below today's price.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, a sign that sales may have been pulled forward or that customers are paying more slowly.
The trend is down: the price is far below the 50-day average of 208.86, no support zone sits below 145.98, and a CEO exit and growing legal exposure are reported.

levels.what: Top of the zone that was support and is now resistance. A close above it repairs the break and returns the call to hold.
The model value at 20% starting growth. Holding above it means the market again prices the business as fairly valued if the margin holds.
The value if operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 113.77 if next-year estimates hold near 16.61, because that price already allows for a large margin decline.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now', but the committee says 'Hold' and the macro and technical views are negative. Yesterday's note set a close below the support zone as the signal to wait, and it fired. Most of the value case depends on a margin that the filings flag as a peak.

swing.why: There is no support level below the price to place a stop under. The 147.57 resistance sits less than one ATR (average daily range, 9.88) above the price, and options imply volatility of 62.0 against 51.1 realized. No trade until a close above 163.9 reclaims the second resistance zone.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in our data, the next catalysts are the 2026-11-20 options expiry, where the 150-strike puts (51,032 open contracts) can add volatility around the old support, and the next quarterly filing, which will show whether receivables and margin hold.

change_mind: A close above 150.03 would move the call back to hold. If a filing also shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing no faster than sales, the call would move to add.
If next year's earnings estimate falls back below 15.91 (its level 30 days ago), the growth case is weakening, and the call would move from wait to avoid.
If the price reaches 113.77 while next-year estimates stay near 16.61, the price already allows for a 48% margin, and the call would move to buy.
payload.what_changed: Changed: from hold to wait, because the close at 145.98 fell below the 147.57 bottom of yesterday's support zone, the failure trigger set in yesterday's note.
